### Problem: Open the Lock {#sec-gr-p4-lock}

A lock has four circular wheels, each showing a digit. A move rolls one wheel by one slot, up or down. `deadends` are codes that jam the lock the moment they are displayed. Start at `0000`. Return the fewest moves that display `target`, or $-1$.

**Graph model.** $10^4$ vertices, one per code. Each has eight neighbours. A deadend is a vertex the search refuses to enter. If `0000` itself is dead, the answer is $-1$ before the queue starts. If the target is `0000`, the answer is $0$.

**Invariants.** The digit $g$ moves to $(g + 1) \bmod 10$ or $(g + 9) \bmod 10$. The second of those is the downward roll. In C++ `(g - 1) % 10` is negative when $g = 0$, and it is not the digit $9$.

**Approaches.**

1. **Breadth-first search** — distance array of length $10000$. $O(10^4 \cdot 8)$.
2. **Two frontiers** — grow the smaller of the start side and the target side by one full layer, and stop when a neighbour sits in the other side. Same answer, fewer states expanded when the target is close to the start and the dead set is large.

#### Breadth-first search

::: {.form-next}
Store a code as an integer $0..9999$. The place values are $1000, 100, 10, 1$.
:::

```{python}

#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lock", "bfs")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def open_lock(deadends, target):
    dead = {int(s) for s in deadends}
    if 0 in dead:
        return -1
    tgt = int(target)
    if tgt == 0:
        return 0
    P = (1000, 100, 10, 1)
    dist = [-1] * 10000
    dist[0] = 0
    q = deque([0])
    while q:
        x = q.popleft()
        cur = x
        for w in range(4):
            g = cur // P[w] % 10
            for step in (1, 9):
                ng = (g + step) % 10
                y = x + (ng - g) * P[w]
                if y in dead or dist[y] != -1:
                    continue
                dist[y] = dist[x] + 1
                if y == tgt:
                    return dist[y]
                q.append(y)
    return -1


dead1 = ["0201", "0101", "0102", "1212", "2002"]
dead3 = ["8887", "8889", "8878", "8898", "8788", "8988", "7888", "9888"]
assert open_lock(dead1, "0202") == 6
assert open_lock(["8888"], "0009") == 1
assert open_lock(dead3, "8888") == -1
assert open_lock([], "0000") == 0
assert open_lock(["0000"], "8888") == -1
assert open_lock([], "5555") == 20
```

##### C++

```cpp
int openLock(vector<string>& deadends, string target) {
    vector<char> dead(10000);
    for (auto& s : deadends) dead[stoi(s)] = 1;
    if (dead[0]) return -1;
    int tgt = stoi(target);
    if (tgt == 0) return 0;
    vector<int> dist(10000, -1);
    queue<int> q;
    dist[0] = 0;
    q.push(0);
    int P[4] = {1000, 100, 10, 1};
    while (!q.empty()) {
        int x = q.front();
        q.pop();
        for (int w = 0; w < 4; w++) {
            int g = x / P[w] % 10;
            for (int step : {1, 9}) {
                int ng = (g + step) % 10;
                int y = x + (ng - g) * P[w];
                if (dead[y] || dist[y] != -1) continue;
                dist[y] = dist[x] + 1;
                if (y == tgt) return dist[y];
                q.push(y);
            }
        }
    }
    return -1;
}
```

:::

#### Two frontiers

::: {.form-next}
Each round expands every state currently in the smaller frontier. The first neighbour that already has a distance on the other side closes a shortest path, because that whole frontier sits at one distance.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lock", "bi")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def open_lock_bi(deadends, target):
    dead = {int(s) for s in deadends}
    if 0 in dead:
        return -1
    tgt = int(target)
    if tgt == 0:
        return 0
    if tgt in dead:
        return -1
    P = (1000, 100, 10, 1)

    def neigh(x):
        out = []
        for w in range(4):
            g = x // P[w] % 10
            for step in (1, 9):
                ng = (g + step) % 10
                out.append(x + (ng - g) * P[w])
        return out

    fa = {0: 0}
    fb = {tgt: 0}
    qa, qb = deque([0]), deque([tgt])
    while qa and qb:
        if len(qa) > len(qb):
            qa, qb = qb, qa
            fa, fb = fb, fa
        for _ in range(len(qa)):
            x = qa.popleft()
            for y in neigh(x):
                if y in dead or y in fa:
                    continue
                if y in fb:
                    return fa[x] + 1 + fb[y]
                fa[y] = fa[x] + 1
                qa.append(y)
    return -1


assert open_lock_bi(dead1, "0202") == 6
assert open_lock_bi(["8888"], "0009") == 1
assert open_lock_bi(dead3, "8888") == -1
assert open_lock_bi([], "0000") == 0
assert open_lock_bi([], "5555") == 20
for _ in range(15):
    tgt = f"{random.randint(0, 9999):04d}"
    dead = [f"{random.randint(0, 9999):04d}" for _ in range(5)]
    assert open_lock(dead, tgt) == open_lock_bi(dead, tgt)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int openLockBi(vector<string>& deadends, string target) {
    vector<char> dead(10000);
    for (auto& s : deadends) dead[stoi(s)] = 1;
    if (dead[0]) return -1;
    int tgt = stoi(target);
    if (tgt == 0) return 0;
    if (dead[tgt]) return -1;
    int P[4] = {1000, 100, 10, 1};
    auto neigh = [&](int x, int out[]) {
        int k = 0;
        for (int w = 0; w < 4; w++) {
            int g = x / P[w] % 10;
            for (int step : {1, 9}) {
                int ng = (g + step) % 10;
                out[k++] = x + (ng - g) * P[w];
            }
        }
    };
    vector<int> fa(10000, -1), fb(10000, -1);
    queue<int> qa, qb;
    fa[0] = 0;
    fb[tgt] = 0;
    qa.push(0);
    qb.push(tgt);
    while (!qa.empty() && !qb.empty()) {
        if (qa.size() > qb.size()) {
            swap(qa, qb);
            swap(fa, fb);
        }
        int layer = qa.size();
        while (layer--) {
            int x = qa.front();
            qa.pop();
            int ys[8];
            neigh(x, ys);
            for (int y : ys) {
                if (dead[y] || fa[y] != -1) continue;
                if (fb[y] != -1) return fa[x] + 1 + fb[y];
                fa[y] = fa[x] + 1;
                qa.push(y);
            }
        }
    }
    return -1;
}
```

:::

:::

**Worked trace.** Target `0009` with a deadend far away: the units wheel rolls from $0$ to $9$ in one downward move, distance $1$. Target `8888` whose eight neighbours are all dead: every entrance is jammed, so the search never pushes `8888`.

**Edge cases.** Target `0000` returns $0$ even when other codes are dead, provided the start itself is open. Start dead returns $-1$. Target `5555` with no deadends takes $20$ rolls, five on each wheel.

**Pitfalls.** `(g - 1) % 10` in C++ yields a negative residue at digit $0$, and the place-value update writes the wrong code. Stopping a bidirectional search in the middle of a layer, after expanding only part of a frontier whose states have different distances, can report a longer route; the form above expands a whole layer of one distance. Forgetting to refuse `0000` when it is dead returns $0$ on a lock that is already jammed.

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- **A downward roll with a negative remainder.** The digit $g$ moves to $(g + 1) \bmod 10$ or $(g + 9) \bmod 10$. At $g = 0$ the second of those is $9$. A C++ remainder of a negative number is not that digit, and the place-value update writes a different code.
- **The start is dead.** If `0000` is a deadend, return $-1$ before the queue starts. Pushing it walks away from a jammed lock.
- **Dead codes checked only at the target.** A dead code in the middle of a route is a deleted vertex. It must never enter the queue.
- **Returning in the middle of a mixed layer.** States in one frontier of this search share a distance, so the first touch is a shortest path. A frontier whose states sit at different distances can report a longer route; expand a whole layer of one distance.
:::

**Variants.** Two jugs, with fill, empty, and pour, are [LC 365 · Water and Jug Problem](https://leetcode.com/problems/water-and-jug-problem/){difficulty="Medium"}: the state is the pair of amounts. One integer and the moves $\pm a_i$ and bitwise xor, staying inside a bounded range, is [LC 2059 · Minimum Operations to Convert Number](https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-operations-to-convert-number/){difficulty="Medium"}. More wheels are the same search on a larger code. Turning two adjacent wheels together only adds neighbours. A wheel with its own cost is a weighted graph.

Source: [LC 752 · Open the Lock](https://leetcode.com/problems/open-the-lock/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
